flashcard_questions.q: How does direct current flow around a circuit?
flashcard_questions.a: In one direction only, at a constant size.

flashcard_questions.q: How does alternating current behave in a circuit?
What is the potential difference of the UK mains supply?
What is the frequency of the UK mains supply?
What colour is the live wire in a UK three-pin plug?
What colour is the neutral wire in a UK three-pin plug?
What colour is the earth wire in a UK three-pin plug?
What does the earth wire do if a fault makes a metal casing live?
flashcard_questions.a: It gives a low-resistance path to earth, so the fuse blows.

flashcard_questions.q: How does a fuse break a circuit when the current is too large?
flashcard_questions.a: Its thin wire heats up and melts.

flashcard_questions.q: How does a circuit breaker differ from a fuse?
flashcard_questions.a: It trips and can be reset, rather than melting.

flashcard_questions.q: Why will a 3 A fuse not protect a person from electrocution?
flashcard_questions.a: About 0.1 A can stop a heart, far below the fuse rating.

flashcard_questions.q: P = ____ × ____, where P is power in watts.
Which equation gives power from current and resistance?
E = ____ × ____, where E is energy transferred in joules.
Why does the National Grid transmit electricity at very high voltage?
flashcard_questions.a: High voltage means low current, so less energy is wasted heating the cables.

notes: 15 cards: 2 cloze on the power and energy equations plus 1 equation-recall card (P = I²R), 2 value-and-unit cards for the mains supply, 3 colour→wire cards with distinct answers, 4 safety-mechanism cards (earth wire, fuse melting, circuit breaker reset, National Grid voltage), 2 current-type behaviour cards, 1 misconception correction on fuses and electrocution. Dropped both worked examples as calculation practice, and the step-down transformer output was cut because its answer (230 V) would collide with the mains supply card.
